title: Automatic boundedness of homomorphisms of strict affinoid algebras
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $A,B\ne0$ be commutative unital $K$-algebras, each with a Tate quotient Banach norm from an affinoid quotient presentation [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. Every unital $K$-algebra homomorphism $f:A\to B$ is bounded: there is a real $D>0$ such that $\|f(a)\|_B\le D\|a\|_A$ for every $a\in A$. In particular $f$ is continuous. No finite-module, injectivity, reducedness, or separability assumption on $f$ is required.

source.place: Theorem 1.2.6(2), printed p.6 (PDF p.6); also Kedlaya tate-algebras.pdf, Corollary 11 and Proposition 10, PDF p.7. Strict affinoid algebras only. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copies WANTED.

proof.text: Choose the given presentations $T_r\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $T_s\twoheadrightarrow B$. Apply [lem-trf-affinoid-polynomial-closed-point-comparison] with polynomial ideal $J=0$ to see that each Tate algebra is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] to the two presentations; hence $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian. Their norms and completeness are already assumptions; no continuity of $f$ has been used.

source.place: Proposition 10 and Corollary 11, PDF p.7; agent reconstruction, using powers of maximal ideals for the separating family and citing every analytic input. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Every ideal $I$ of either algebra $C=A,B$ is closed. Indeed Noetherianity means that $I=(c_1,\ldots,c_t)$ by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The map $C^t\to C$, $(a_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_ic_i$, is $C$-linear with image $I$. Both modules are finite and complete with their maximum norms, and their $C$-actions satisfy the required bound with constant $1$ by submultiplicativity. Thus [lem-trf-affinoid-finite-module-strictness] says its image is closed. Coordinatewise Cauchy limits give completeness of $C^t$; $t=0$ handles $I=0$.

source.place: Proposition 10 and Corollary 11, PDF p.7; agent reconstruction, using powers of maximal ideals for the separating family and citing every analytic input. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset B$, [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus], applied to the nonzero algebra $B$ with its given surjective $K$-algebra presentation $T_s\twoheadrightarrow B$, says that the field $B/\mathfrak m$ is finite over $K$. Apply [lem-trf-noetherian-residue-finite-quotients] to the Noetherian algebra $B$ (step 1). The ideals $I=\mathfrak m^n$, for all maximal $\mathfrak m$ and $n\ge1$, have finite-dimensional quotients $B/I$ and their intersection is zero. Write $\mathcal S$ for this family.

source.place: Proposition 10 and Corollary 11, PDF p.7; agent reconstruction, using powers of maximal ideals for the separating family and citing every analytic input. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $I\in\mathcal S$ and put $J=f^{-1}(I)$. This is an ideal of $A$, closed by step 2, as is $I$ in $B$. The formula $\bar f_I:A/J\to B/I$, $a+J\mapsto f(a)+I$, is well-defined, $K$-linear and injective: its kernel consists precisely of the cosets of elements of $J$. Since $B/I$ is finite-dimensional, so is $A/J$: the images of any linearly independent list remain independent, so a list cannot have length exceeding a finite basis of $B/I$.

source.place: Proposition 10 and Corollary 11, PDF p.7; agent reconstruction, using powers of maximal ideals for the separating family and citing every analytic input. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Equip $A/J$ and $B/I$ with their vector-space quotient topologies. By [lem-trf-closed-subspace-hausdorff-quotient] these are Hausdorff topological $K$-vector spaces. The field $K$ is complete and nontrivially valued, so [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous] applies to $\bar f_I$ and proves it continuous. The quotient maps are continuous by [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-quotient-open]. Consequently $h_I:A\to B/I$, $a\mapsto f(a)+I$, is continuous, since $h_I=\bar f_I\circ q_J$. This does not assume that $f$ is continuous.

source.place: Proposition 10 and Corollary 11, PDF p.7; agent reconstruction, using powers of maximal ideals for the separating family and citing every analytic input. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $a_j\to a$ in $A$ and $f(a_j)\to b$ in $B$. For each $I\in\mathcal S$, continuity proved in step 5 shows $h_I(a_j)\to h_I(a)$ and $q_I(f(a_j))\to q_I(b)$. These are the same sequence in the Hausdorff space $B/I$, so uniqueness of limits gives $f(a)+I=b+I$. Hence $b-f(a)\in I$ for every $I\in\mathcal S$, and step 3 gives $b=f(a)$. The sequential criterion of [lem-trf-banach-closed-graph-continuity] now proves $f$ continuous: a unital $K$-algebra homomorphism is $K$-linear, and $A,B$ are complete normed $K$-spaces by assumption.

source.place: Proposition 10 and Corollary 11, PDF p.7; agent reconstruction, using powers of maximal ideals for the separating family and citing every analytic input. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-continuous-linear-map-norm-bound] to this continuous $K$-linear map to obtain $D>0$ with $\|f(a)\|_B\le D\|a\|_A$ for all $a$. Nontriviality of the absolute value is exactly the hypothesis of that norm-bound lemma. The argument used neither injectivity nor finiteness of $f$, and the separating family uses all maximal-ideal powers, so it did not assume reducedness or separability.
